size.note: No size figures published specifically for Genetta felina were found. Head-and-body length (43–55 cm) and tail (33–52 cm) follow the Wikipedia account of the common genet (Genetta genetta). Mass of 1–3 kg follows Animal Diversity Web for G. genetta; a male average of 2 kg on Wikipedia is omitted as an average. These figures are for G. genetta broadly, not confirmed for G. felina itself.

summary: A slender, nocturnal genet with small spots, dark feet, a dark chin and a white-tipped, strongly ringed tail. In this guide it is stored as Genetta felina, a southern African split from the common genet Genetta genetta.
description: The small-spotted genet is a lightly built, short-legged viverrid with a long, strongly ringed tail. In Genetta felina the tail has a white tip, the feet are dark, and the chin is dark. The coat is spotted with small, fairly neat marks. Sexes are similar in colour. EWT still assesses the group as Genetta genetta and notes that the status of G. felina is debated. Photographs in this file are identified as G. felina, not as G. genetta or G. tigrina.
habits: It is nocturnal, usually solitary, and often partly arboreal, hunting and resting in trees as well as on the ground. Like other small genets it is an opportunistic feeder.

diet.summary: An opportunistic feeder, taking small vertebrates, insects and fruit. The diet account follows general common-genet sources, not a Kruger-specific study.

young: In the common genet, young are born in the wet season after a gestation of about 10–11 weeks, in litters of 1–3, and are born blind. A source giving birth months specifically for Genetta felina in Kruger was not found.
habitat: Woodland, riverine trees and the edges of rest camps. It is widespread but secretive, and is most often seen at night.

similar.note: The large-spotted genet has larger, often rusty or blotched spots and a dark tail tip, not a white one, and it lacks dark feet and a dark chin.
The African civet is much larger and heavier, with a deep chest, a bold black-and-white face and black legs.

viewNotes.note: In a tree, the long, strongly ringed tail with a white tip is the clearest mark that separates this species from the large-spotted genet.
Small spots, dark feet and a white tail tip distinguish it from the large-spotted genet.

calls.description: In the common genet, kits moan or mew, and adults may growl or give a click as a threat. A field description specifically for Genetta felina was not found.
